content.title: What are Functional Interfaces?
content.description: A Functional Interface is an interface that contains exactly one abstract method. It serves as the foundation for Lambda Expressions and the functional programming features introduced in Java 8.

content.content: Functional interfaces enable Java to support functional programming. They allow behavior to be passed as data through Lambda Expressions and Method References. Although a functional interface contains only one abstract method, it can also have any number of default, static, and private methods.

content.title: Why Functional Interfaces?
content.content: Functional interfaces make code more concise, reusable, readable, and are the backbone of Java's Streams API, Lambda Expressions, and asynchronous programming.
A functional interface must contain exactly one abstract method. However, it may include multiple default methods, static methods, and methods inherited from the Object class.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Every Lambda Expression in Java represents an implementation of a functional interface.

content.content: The @FunctionalInterface annotation is optional but recommended. It tells the compiler that the interface should contain only one abstract method and generates an error if additional abstract methods are added.

content.title: Compiler Safety
content.content: Using @FunctionalInterface helps prevent accidental modification of an interface into a non-functional interface.
Instead of creating anonymous classes, Lambda Expressions provide a concise implementation of the single abstract method.
The java.util.function package provides several predefined functional interfaces for common programming tasks.
Developers can create their own functional interfaces whenever the built-in interfaces do not satisfy application requirements.

items.answer: Implementing listeners using concise lambda expressions.

content.title: Single Responsibility Worker
content.content: Imagine hiring a specialist whose job is to perform exactly one task efficiently. A functional interface similarly defines one specific responsibility through a single abstract method.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Functional interfaces, @FunctionalInterface, Predicate, Function, Consumer, Supplier, Lambda Expressions, Method References, Streams API, and default methods are among the most commonly asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Can a functional interface have multiple abstract methods?
items.answer: No. It must contain exactly one abstract method.

items.question: Are default methods counted as abstract methods?
items.answer: No. Default and static methods do not affect functional interface status.

items.question: Is @FunctionalInterface mandatory?
items.answer: No. It is optional but strongly recommended for compile-time validation.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: A functional interface contains one abstract method and enables Lambda Expressions and functional programming in Java.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: A functional interface contains exactly one abstract method.
Default and static methods are allowed.
Common built-in interfaces include Predicate, Function, Consumer, and Supplier.
Functional interfaces are widely used with Streams and the Executor Framework.
